editorial.headline: Refill Drinking Water, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 11052 covers refill drinking-water production through filtration, from manual depots to automatic tap water machines, and the record keeps both national PMA access and Bali treatment open.
editorial.body:
KBLI 11052 is a practical water-industry activity: the making of drinking water that can be consumed directly through refill depots, whether the depot is operated manually by people or through an automatic tap water machine. The record defines the work as processing raw water into drinking water using filtration equipment. That is the center of the activity, and it is also the limit of what can be said from the record: this code is about producing refill drinking water, not a broader packaged-beverage or distribution narrative.

The registration base is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not confined to one business size. A small refill-water depot and a larger operation can both sit inside the same registered activity, provided the activity remains the one described in the scope: turning raw water into ready-to-drink refill water through filtration, with either manual or automatic filling. That breadth matters because the code reads less like a niche exception and more like an activity designed to cover the ordinary range of refill-drinking-water operations.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this KBLI as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower foreign-equity ceiling in the slim record, and no additional national threshold, capital figure, permit condition, or timing rule is stated here. The honest national reading is therefore simple: for this activity, the record shows a fully open PMA position at national level.

Bali does not add a hidden percentage in this record. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That sits against the stated Bali moratorium rule, under which Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. For this code, however, the record does not mark a Bali block. The accurate reading is that KBLI 11052 is nationally open to PMA and, on the Bali fields provided here, not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
